name: How to Check Driveway Base Preparation Before Installation

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if a driveway contractor is using proper base preparation?
mainEntity.text: How can I tell if a driveway contractor is using proper base preparation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Base preparation is one of the most important parts of a driveway project because the top surface is only as good as the foundation underneath it. Homeowners should expect excavation to the proper depth, removal of soft or unstable material, installation of compacted aggregate or base rock, and grading that supports drainage away from structures. A contractor should be able to describe these steps clearly and include them in the written scope. It is also reasonable to ask for photos during construction, especially before the surface is poured or paved. In Los Angeles County, soil conditions, slope, and drainage can make base work even more important than the finish material. If a contractor talks mostly about the surface appearance and not the foundation, that is a warning sign. Good base prep may not be visible once the driveway is finished, but it is the main factor that helps prevent future settling and cracking.
acceptedAnswer.description: Proper base preparation usually includes excavation to the right depth, compacted aggregate, correct grading, and attention to drainage before the surface is installed. Homeowners can ask for photos, daily progress updates, and a written scope that names the base material and compaction steps. Weak base prep is a common cause of future cracking and settling.
